newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Kissinger says U.S. should avoid provoking China.
newsitem.headline: Kissinger says U.S. should avoid provoking China.

text.p: Former U.S. Secretary of State Henry Kissinger said on Wednesday the United States should give China a stake in world affairs and warned confrontation between Washington and Beijing would have "major consequences."
"As far as the United States is concerned, it is my strong belief that we should not provoke what we fear most," he told a luncheon attended by business, government and diplomatic officials.
"Declaring China an enemy today before they have actually done any expansion and before there has been a direct challenge would have major consequences in which, in my view, we would have no allies."

Kissinger, on a four-day visit to the Philippines, urged the United States to foster "a cooperative but realistic relationship with China, willing to give them a real stake in the international system and welcoming their participation."
Kissinger helped establish U.S. ties with China in the 1970s.
He said the world community should "get used to the reality" of China's growing economic might.
